take: Sugarloaf Social Club runs the widest price range in independent golf and holds a single point of view across all of it. The catalogue reaches from a MacKenzie sailcloth bag at $1,400 down to a paper fan at $14, and both read as the same company. It started as a group chat. A few college roommates were graduating in 2011 and wanted somewhere to keep talking about golf, so they named the thread after the course they had spent four years on. The chat became an annual trip, and the trip became an Instagram account that at one point had more followers than Golf Digest. Ian Gilley filed the LLC in 2017 and has described the sequence as “a happy little accident.”
story_extra: The course they named it after is dead. Sugarloaf Mountain in Minneola, Florida was Coore & Crenshaw's first design in the state, built in 2008 across more than 250 feet of elevation, and it opened directly into the financial crisis. It never recovered and it is permanently closed. A brand named after a course you can no longer play is an on-the-nose metaphor for how golf nostalgia works, and to their credit SSC has never leaned on it.

Sugarloaf is a subsidiary of Pro Shop, Inc., the media company founded by Full Swing producer Chad Mumm and Joe Purzycki, which raised around $20 million from the PGA Tour and Powerhouse Capital and also owns Skratch and GolfWRX. Skratch discloses this in its own coverage. It explains how an independent-looking brand from McLean, Virginia ends up with an officially licensed THE PLAYERS capsule in the navy, gold and white it drew up for TPC Sawgrass.

The catalogue reads as thirty-three projects. MacKenzie bags built from retired sailcloth sit next to a $14 paper fan printed for a Japanese golf media brand, a teal-striped soccer kit made for a coffee bar, and a Western Golf Association line supporting the Evans Scholars program. Most of it has sold out.
